Chapter 8: Giving Back—Mentorship, Advocacy, and the Power of Story
Over time, the young man’s journey begins to shift. Sure, there’s that feeling of accomplishment from his success—on the slopes, and in his career. But as the years go by, something else grows inside him: a sense of responsibility that comes with all that experience. He can’t help but think back to the mentors who guided him, those coaches who believed in him, and the friends who stuck around even when things got tough.
Now, he finds himself looking for ways to give back. He starts saying yes to speaking gigs, visiting schools, and getting involved in mentorship programs. Every time, he meets kids facing their own tough battles—illness, disability, or just feeling like they don’t fit in. He listens, really listens, to their stories. And sometimes, he just offers a simple reminder: you’re not alone, and things can get better.
That’s when he truly sees the power of sharing his story. People aren’t just drawn to the details of what he’s done—they connect with the honesty and vulnerability in how he tells it. He figures out how to inspire without sugarcoating, being real about the tough days as well as the victories. And you know what? Most people crave stories that show both the struggle and the hope.
Naturally, advocacy becomes part of his path. He joins organizations working to open doors for people with disabilities. He pushes for better healthcare, more inclusive sports programs, and real representation in media and public life. The progress? Sometimes it’s slow. Frustrating, even. But little wins matter—a new ramp at the local school, a new scholarship for adaptive athletes, a change in policy that makes someone’s life just a bit easier.
Through it all, he stays rooted in the relationships that mean the most. His partner, family, and close friends help him keep his feet on the ground, reminding him to take care of himself, too. That balance between giving and receiving? It’s a practice, something he works at every day—with humility, and a good dose of self-awareness.
Most folks never realize how much difference a single story can make. For him, every time he shares—whether it’s in front of a big crowd or just one-on-one—it’s a way to honor the journey, and maybe, just maybe, light the way for someone else.
